es: Defender una causa local ante un público y responder a una objeción con respeto, evidencia y una petición final.

vocabulary.es: hacer una pausa para dar fuerza
admitir que el otro tiene razón en algo

teaching.en: Let me be clear: a crossing is not a luxury, it is a need, and we have the figures to prove it.
teaching.es: Seré claro: un paso de peatones no es un lujo, es una necesidad, y tenemos las cifras para demostrarlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Let me be clear introduce la idea central con firmeza; combina bien con un contraste (not… it is).
segments: Let me be clear: a crossing is not a luxury, it
is a need, and we have the figures to prove it.
teaching.audioText: Let me be clear: a crossing is not a luxury, it is a need, and we have the figures to prove it.

teaching.en: I want to address a concern raised by some neighbours: the delay to the traffic would last two minutes, no more.
teaching.es: Quiero atender una preocupación planteada por algunos vecinos: la demora en el tráfico duraría dos minutos, no más.
teaching.explanationEs: Address a concern: nombra la objeción con respeto antes de responderla con un dato.
segments: I want to address a concern raised by some neighbours: the
delay to the traffic would last two minutes, no more.
teaching.audioText: I want to address a concern raised by some neighbours: the delay to the traffic would last two minutes, no more.

teaching.en: That is a fair point, and I am willing to concede it: a crossing will cost money, but one accident would cost far more.
teaching.es: Es un punto razonable y estoy dispuesto a admitirlo: un paso de peatones costará dinero, pero un accidente costaría mucho más.
teaching.explanationEs: Concede a point: admitir lo cierto da credibilidad; luego vuelve a tu argumento con but o however.
segments: That is a fair point, and I am willing to concede it:
a crossing will cost money, but one accident would cost far more.
teaching.audioText: That is a fair point, and I am willing to concede it: a crossing will cost money, but one accident would cost far more.

teaching.en: To rebut an objection, do not reply with anger: acknowledge the worry, answer with evidence and return to your request.
teaching.es: Para rebatir una objeción, no respondas con enfado: reconoce la preocupación, contesta con pruebas y vuelve a tu petición.
teaching.explanationEs: Rebut an objection: tres pasos, reconocer, responder con evidencia y volver a la petición.
segments: To rebut an objection, do not reply with anger: acknowledge
the worry, answer with evidence and return to your request.
teaching.audioText: To rebut an objection, do not reply with anger: acknowledge the worry, answer with evidence and return to your request.

teaching.en: Say the key line slowly and pause for effect before the last word, so that the audience has time to take it in.
teaching.es: Di la frase clave despacio y haz una pausa para dar fuerza antes de la última palabra, para que el público tenga tiempo de asimilarla.
teaching.explanationEs: Pause for effect: el silencio justo antes de la idea clave la hace más memorable.
segments: Say the key line slowly and pause for effect before the last
word, so that the audience has time to take it in.
teaching.audioText: Say the key line slowly and pause for effect before the last word, so that the audience has time to take it in.

teaching.en: Stand your ground without raising your voice: the survey is clear, eighty-two per cent of families want a safer road.
teaching.es: Mantente firme sin levantar la voz: la encuesta es clara, el ochenta y dos por ciento de las familias quiere una calle más segura.
teaching.explanationEs: Stand your ground: firmeza con calma; la evidencia sostiene tu postura, no el volumen.
segments: Stand your ground without raising your voice: the survey is
clear, eighty-two per cent of families want a safer road.
teaching.audioText: Stand your ground without raising your voice: the survey is clear, eighty-two per cent of families want a safer road.

prompt.es: Elige la mejor respuesta de Carlos a la objeción del vecino.

choices.text: I understand your concern, but one accident would cost the town far more than a crossing.
You are wrong, and you clearly do not care about the children who cross this road here.
Everyone agrees with me, so there is really no need to discuss the cost any further.

feedback.es: Reconoce la preocupación y responde con una comparación de costos; las otras dos atacan a la persona o recurren al bandwagon.

hint.es: Busca la respuesta que reconoce la objeción, da una razón y no ataca a nadie.

origin.text: At the meeting, a neighbour says: “A crossing will cost too much, and I doubt the council can afford it.” Carlos must reply in a way that respects the speaker, uses evidence and returns to his request.

prompt.es: Completa: «Seré claro: un paso de peatones no es un lujo, es una necesidad.»

feedback.es: Let me be clear es la fórmula para introducir con firmeza la idea central, antes de dar la prueba.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo que significa «sin ambigüedad» y aparece en la fórmula let me be…

origin.text: Some of you did not understand my point. Let me be ___: a crossing is not a luxury, it is a need, and the survey proves it.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es un punto justo, pero los niños van primero.»

answer.text: That is a fair point, but children come first

feedback.es: Se admite el punto con that is a fair point y se vuelve al argumento con but.

hint.es: Empieza con That is y termina con come first.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo responde la oradora a la objeción del tráfico.

choices.text: She rejects the worry at once and answers with figures alone.
She accepts the worry and answers with a comparison and data.
She accepts the worry and agrees that the crossing should be postponed.

feedback.es: Acepta la preocupación («I understand the concern»), compara dos minutos de demora con la seguridad de un niño y aporta la encuesta.

origin.audio: Some neighbours say a crossing will slow the traffic, and I understand the concern. However, two minutes of delay is nothing next to a child's safety. The survey is clear: eighty-two per cent of families want it. So I ask you tonight to support a safer road for everyone.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que marca mejor con énfasis el momento clave del discurso.

choices.text: The cost is important, and the child is important, and so is everything else.
Perhaps it is fair to say that the child may matter more than the cost.
What matters most is not the cost; it is the child who crosses.

feedback.es: El cleft con what y el contraste not… it is ponen el foco en el niño; las otras frases reparten la atención o la diluyen con dudas.

origin.text: Carlos wants to stress that a child's safety matters more than the cost. He has two minutes left and must choose the most forceful sentence for the end of his speech.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su función en la respuesta.

pairs: The council's own survey shows 82% support.
That is a fair point, and I concede it.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta encadena reconocimiento, evidencia, una concesión honesta y la petición final.

pairs: The council's own survey shows 82% support.
That is a fair point, and I concede it.

prompt.es: Decide si lo que dice este orador es argumento o presión.

choices.text: Misleading: it mixes a false dilemma, the bandwagon and false urgency.
Legitimate: its urgency is justified because so many neighbours have already signed.
Misleading, but only because it lacks a survey; its tone is otherwise fair.

feedback.es: «Sign now, or you are against» es un falso dilema, «everyone has signed» es bandwagon y «no time to read» es falsa urgencia: presión, no argumento.

origin.text: Speaker at the meeting: “Sign now, or you are against our children! Everyone in this street has already signed, and there is no time to read the petition.”

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nunca antes tantos padres habían pedido un paso de peatones.»

answer.text: Never before have so many parents asked for a crossing

feedback.es: Never before va al inicio y el auxiliar have pasa delante del sujeto so many parents.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué busca la oradora al contrastar «minor delay» y «matter of life».

choices.text: To concede that the delay is minor while asking the audience to stay calm.
To show that the council treats a serious risk as a small thing.
To ask the audience to choose between the council and her.

feedback.es: Al oponer «minor delay» a «matter of life», la oradora da a entender que el ayuntamiento resta importancia a un riesgo grave.

origin.audio: Who will speak for a child who cannot vote? This year, three children almost had an accident at our school gate. The council calls it a minor delay; I call it a matter of life. And I will say this slowly, because it matters: a crossing is not a luxury. It is a need.

prompt.es: Escribe tu discurso por el paso de peatones y responde a dos objeciones.

answer.text: Who will speak for a child who cannot vote? This year, three children almost had an accident at our school gate. What we need is a safe crossing. Our survey is clear: 82% of families support it. Some of you may say it will cost too much. I understand your concern, but one accident would cost far more. Others say it will cause a delay to the traffic. That is a fair point; however, two minutes of delay is nothing next to a child's safety. Never before have so many parents asked for something so simple. It is our children who cross that road every morning, and it is we who must protect them. Let me be clear: a crossing is not a luxury, it is a need. I do not ask you for a favour; I ask you for what every child in this town deserves, and I ask you to stand with me tonight. So please sign the petition before Friday, because our children cannot wait.
accepted: Who will speak for a child who cannot vote? This year, three children almost had an accident at our school gate. What we need is a safe crossing. Our survey is clear: 82% of families support it. Some of you may say it will cost too much. I understand your concern, but one accident would cost far more. Others say it will cause a delay to the traffic. That is a fair point; however, two minutes of delay is nothing next to a child's safety. Never before have so many parents asked for something so simple. It is our children who cross that road every morning, and it is we who must protect them. Let me be clear: a crossing is not a luxury, it is a need. I do not ask you for a favour; I ask you for what every child in this town deserves, and I ask you to stand with me tonight. So please sign the petition before Friday, because our children cannot wait.

Imagine a child crossing our road every morning. Three of them almost had an accident this year. A survey found that 82% of families want a safe crossing. I understand the concern about the cost, but one accident would cost much more. It is true that the traffic will slow down; however, two minutes of delay is nothing next to a life. What we need is action, and never before have so many parents asked for it. It is our children who cross that road every morning, and it is we who must protect them. Despite the delay, children will be safer, and the survey shows that families agree. Let me be clear: we will not stop asking. Please sign the petition before Friday.

feedback.es: El discurso completo lleva gancho, dato de la encuesta, énfasis, respuesta a las dos objeciones y una petición con fecha.

origin.text: Datos: paso de peatones seguro frente a la escuela. Este año, tres niños casi fueron atropellados. Una encuesta halló que el 82 % de las familias lo apoya. Objeciones: «cuesta demasiado» y «retrasará el tráfico». Petición final: firmar la petición antes del viernes. Incluye gancho, dato, dos recursos de énfasis, respuesta a las dos objeciones y una petición final.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la oradora empieza respondiendo con «I hear that concern».

choices.text: To avoid the question by changing the subject to the survey.
To admit that the objection is right and stop asking for signatures.
To show respect for the objection before answering it with evidence.

feedback.es: Reconocer la objeción («I hear that concern») antes de responder con la encuesta muestra respeto y da credibilidad a su postura.

origin.audio: A question came from the back of the hall: is a crossing not a waste of public money? The speaker took a breath and paused. Nobody moved, and she did not raise her voice once. I hear that concern, she said, and I will not pretend that money is no object. But the survey is clear: eighty-two per cent of parents feel afraid at the gate, and three children were almost hurt there this year. So please sign before Friday.

prompt.es: Completa: «La frase clave se lee despacio, palabra por palabra.»

feedback.es: Slowly es el adverbio que describe cómo leer la frase clave: despacio, palabra por palabra, para que el público la asimile.

origin.text: Nobody should rush the most important sentence of a speech. Sara took a breath and read it ___, one word at a time, so that nobody missed a single word.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que usa despite correctamente.

choices.text: Despite the delay, children will be safer.
Despite of the delay, children will be safer.
In spite the delay, children will be safer.

feedback.es: Despite va seguido directamente del sustantivo: despite the delay. Despite of es un error, y in spite necesita of (in spite of).

origin.text: Carlos wants to say that, even though the crossing will cause a short delay, children will be safer. He is not sure which word must come next.
